title: Vranec & Stanušina: The Tikveš Basin and the Vardar Road
subRegion: Tikveš & Povardarie, Kavadarci, Negotino, Demir Kapija, Štip & Skopje

bestPeriod.avoid: July-mid-August, the Tikveš basin is the hottest place in the country at 38-42°C with almost no shade

food.note: Restaurant mains MKD 350-700 (€6, €11); a full winery dinner MKD 1,500-2,500 (€24, €41)

transport.note: Rental car 6 days, fuel, one driver day, Skopje taxis

activities.note: Tastings MKD 600-1,800 (€10, €29), Stobi entry, ajvar session, rakija visit

profile.difficultyNote: 2/5, vineyard walking, the Stobi site on gravel, a short climb at Marko's Towers

gatewayAirport: SKP Skopje, 1 h 20 min drive to Negotino, 1 h 35 min to Kavadarci; OHD Ohrid 2 h 30 min
summary: Tikveš is the largest continuous vineyard region in the Balkans and almost nobody visits it. The basin sits between the Vardar and the Kožuf mountains, gets around 270 sunny days a year, and grows Vranec, the black, tannic national grape, alongside Stanušina, a pale indigenous red found nowhere else. The week runs south from Skopje through Negotino, Kavadarci and Demir Kapija, staying in wineries that built their own rooms because there were no hotels, then east to Štip for pastrmajlija. Come in September and the whole country is outdoors making ajvar over open fires.

itinerary.title: Skopje: Bit Pazar and the Old Bazaar
itinerary.morning: Land at SKP, 20 minutes from the centre. Walk the Stone Bridge into the **Old Bazaar**, the largest surviving Ottoman bazaar in the Balkans outside Istanbul.
itinerary.afternoon: **Bit Pazar**, pepper mountains in September, ajvar pots, dried beans for tavče gravče, sheep cheese, rakija sold by the funnel.
itinerary.evening: **Pivnica An** in a restored caravanserai for kebapi and tavče gravče, or **Stara Kuća** for the fuller spread.
itinerary.dayStats: SKP 20 min / bazaar meal MKD 400-800 (€7, €13) / market ajvar 1 kg jar MKD 300-500 (€5, €8) / no driving today

itinerary.title: South to Stobi and Negotino
itinerary.morning: The A1 down the Vardar to **Stobi**, the Roman and early Byzantine city at the Crna-Vardar confluence, mosaics, a theatre, the Episcopal basilica, and effectively empty midweek.
itinerary.afternoon: **Stobi Winery** next door for a first Vranec and a Temjanika, then on to **Bovin** at Negotino, the country's first private winery.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Popova Kula on arrival at Demir Kapija; the kitchen pairs the winery's own range.
itinerary.dayStats: 95 km Skopje-Stobi, 1 h 10 m / Stobi entry MKD 120-300 (€2, €5) / 2 wineries / tastings MKD 600-1,500 (€10, €24) each

itinerary.title: Demir Kapija and the Stanušina question
itinerary.morning: **Popova Kula**'s own tasting, working through Vranec, Kratošija, Temjanika and, the reason to be here, **Stanušina** as both a light red and a rosé.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Demir Kapija** gorge, the "iron gate" where the Vardar cuts through the mountains, then the winery's collection of dozens of local varieties grown side by side.
itinerary.evening: Stay in; Demir Kapija has little else, which is exactly why the winery built rooms.
itinerary.dayStats: 1 winery / Keif-style tasting MKD 900-1,800 (€15, €29) / Stanušina bottle MKD 500-900 (€8, €15) / no driving

itinerary.title: Kavadarci, Tikveš Winery and Lake Tikveš
itinerary.morning: Driver day. **Tikveš Winery** at Kavadarci, founded 1885, the largest in south-east Europe, and its Barovo and Lepovo single-vineyard programme.
itinerary.afternoon: Out to **Lake Tikveš**, the reservoir on the Crna, for a boat hour and the vineyard slopes above it.
itinerary.evening: A Kavadarci kafana for tavče gravče baked to order in its earthenware dish, and a carafe of house Vranec.
itinerary.dayStats: 32 km / 1 winery / tasting MKD 700-1,600 (€11, €26) / driver day €150, €280 per car / Vranec Reserve MKD 700-1,400 (€11, €23)

itinerary.title: Ajvar over the fire, and rakija
itinerary.morning: In September, the hands-on morning: an **ajvar session**, crates of red peppers roasted over an open grill, peeled hot, minced and slow-cooked in oil for hours. Arranged through your host, not sold as a tour.
itinerary.afternoon: A **rakija distillation** visit in a Tikveš village if you are here in October or November; otherwise a cellar visit at **Lazar Winery** or **Château Sopot**.
itinerary.evening: Eat what you made. Ajvar with sheep cheese, bread and grilled meat is the correct end to the day.
itinerary.dayStats: Ajvar session 4-6 h / ~10 kg peppers yields ~3 kg ajvar / rakija 40-50% abv / visit fees MKD 500-1,200 (€8, €20)

itinerary.title: East to Štip for pastrmajlija
itinerary.morning: Drive north-east to **Štip**, the textile city on the Bregalnica, and climb to the **Isar** fortress above it.
itinerary.afternoon: Pastrmajlija from a dedicated *pastrmajlijarnica*, the oval bread with cubed pork and a cracked egg, ordered by size and eaten with a hot pepper and a beer.
itinerary.evening: Back west toward Skopje, or a night in Štip. Stop at **Chateau Kamnik** on the Skopje approach for a last serious tasting.
itinerary.dayStats: 105 km Demir Kapija-Štip, 1 h 30 m / pastrmajlija MKD 200-400 (€3, €7) / Kamnik tasting MKD 900-1,800 (€15, €29)

itinerary.title: Matka, last market, and out
itinerary.morning: **Matka Canyon**, 30 minutes from Skopje, a gorge, a reservoir and Vrelo cave, and the country's easiest morning off.
itinerary.afternoon: Last buys at Bit Pazar: ajvar, dried peppers, sheep cheese and a bottle of Stanušina that will be almost impossible to find at home.
itinerary.evening: SKP is 25 minutes from the centre. Wine over one litre goes in the hold; there are duty limits leaving for the EU.
itinerary.dayStats: Matka 30 min each way / boat to Vrelo MKD 300-600 (€5, €10) / SKP 25 min / EU duty allowance 4 l still wine per adult

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Popova Kula
accommodationStrategy.description: A hilltop winery with around 25 rooms, a restaurant and terrace over the Vardar gorge, and a variety collection of indigenous grapes in the grounds. Tasting, dinner and bed in one building solves the driving problem for three nights. MKD 3,700-6,200 (€60, €100) double.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Solun
accommodationStrategy.description: Central, walkable to the Old Bazaar and Bit Pazar, with parking, the practical bookend for the first and last nights. MKD 3,000-5,000 (€49, €81).

accommodationStrategy.name: Tikveš Winery guest accommodation / Kavadarci town hotels
accommodationStrategy.description: If you want to be inside the vineyard basin rather than at its southern edge, Kavadarci has plain, cheap town hotels and Tikveš's own estates offer limited guest capacity, book by email, as online listings are patchy. MKD 2,500-4,500 (€40, €73).

logistics.connectivity: **Non-EU, so EU roaming does not apply**, check your operator's Western Balkans tariff or buy a local A1 or Telekom prepaid SIM at the airport for a few euros. 4G coverage is good along the Vardar corridor and in the towns, weaker in the Kožuf foothills.
logistics.emergency: 112, plus 192 police, 193 fire, 194 ambulance. Main hospitals are in Skopje; Kavadarci and Negotino have clinics only. **EHIC/GHIC does not apply**, full travel insurance with medical repatriation is essential.
logistics.weather: The basin is the hottest, driest part of the country, 38-42°C in July and August with no shade in the vineyards. The **Vardarec**, a cold northerly funnelled down the valley, drops temperatures sharply in winter and spring.
logistics.bookingWindows: Popova Kula rooms 2-4 weeks, longer in September. Tikveš, Stobi and Kamnik visits a week by email. Ajvar and rakija sessions are arranged informally through your host, not booked online. Skopje hotels a few days.
logistics.money: The currency is the **Macedonian denar (MKD)**, pegged at roughly **61.5 MKD to €1**. Cards work in Skopje, wineries and larger restaurants; markets, village kafanas and rural fuel stations are cash. Withdraw denars from ATMs rather than changing euros at the airport, and do not accumulate denars, they are hard to change back. Tipping is 10%.
logistics.transportRules: Blood-alcohol 0.5 g/l, **0.0 for drivers with under two years' licence and professionals**; on-the-spot fines are normal. A **green card** is required for a car brought from abroad, and most EU rental agreements prohibit or surcharge entry into North Macedonia, hire locally in Skopje instead. The A1 is tolled in short sections, cash or card, and Skopje-Gevgelija tolls total a few euros. Headlights on at all times.
logistics.permits: North Macedonia is outside the EU and the Schengen area, so there is a **customs border**, the EU duty allowance on return is 4 litres of still wine and 1 litre of spirits per adult, and larger wine purchases must be declared. **Wild Ohrid trout is protected**; buying or ordering it is not something to encourage.
logistics.health: Tap water is drinkable in Skopje and the main towns; use bottled in villages. Rakija is 40-50% abv and is poured as hospitality rather than as a drink you ordered. Summer sun in the basin is severe and vineyards offer no shade.

proTips: Ask for Stanušina at every winery, even when it is not on the tasting list. It grows nowhere else, several producers make only a few thousand bottles, and it is the single thing you cannot buy at home.
Taste Vranec and Kratošija side by side. Kratošija is Zinfandel under another name, and the comparison instantly explains why Vranec tastes as black and structured as it does.
Book the winery that has rooms. Tikveš has almost no hotel infrastructure and Popova Kula's model, cellar, kitchen and bed in one building, is the only way to drink properly without a driver.
Go in September for ajvar. Every household in the basin is roasting peppers outdoors, and being invited to help is genuinely easy if you ask your host rather than an agency.
Buy a local SIM at Skopje airport. EU roaming does not reach North Macedonia and a week of data costs a couple of euros against potentially punitive roaming charges.

Do not hire the car in Greece or Bulgaria and drive in. Most EU rental contracts exclude North Macedonia or charge a heavy cross-border fee; renting in Skopje is cheaper and avoids the green-card problem entirely.
Eat pastrmajlija in Štip rather than Skopje. It is a Štip dish, the ovens there are set up for it, and the version sold in the capital is a pale copy.

raw.Appellation structure: The wine law divides the country into three regions and sixteen districts; **Povardarie** (the Vardar River Valley) is the largest and contains the **Tikveš** district, which alone makes roughly two-thirds of national production. The PDO/PGI framework is being aligned to EU practice under accession, so labels carry *kontrolirano poteklo* rather than a DOC-style term, expect "Tikveš" as the geographical claim.
raw.Grapes: **Vranec** ("black stallion") is the flagship: deep, tannic, 14%+, ageing well in oak. **Kratošija** is the same variety as Zinfandel and Primitivo and gives a rounder, redder-fruited wine. **Stanušina** is endemic to Tikveš, pale, low-tannin, high-acid, made as a light red and a rosé, and effectively unavailable outside the country. Whites: **Temjanika** (Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains) is the aromatic star, **Smederevka** the high-acid workhorse.
raw.Wineries with rooms and how to book: **Popova Kula** at **Demir Kapija** is the model, a hilltop winery with a hotel, restaurant and a variety collection including Stanušina, with structured tastings and email booking, English fluent; the "Keif" style tastings and dinner-plus-room packages are its published formats. **Tikveš Winery** at **Kavadarci**, founded 1885 and the largest in south-east Europe, runs a visitor programme at its Barovo and Lepovo estates. **Stobi Winery** near **Gradsko** has a modern visitor centre beside the archaeological site; **Chateau Kamnik** near Skopje, **Bovin** at Negotino (the first private winery) and **Lazar Winery** complete the list. Most want a **week's email notice**; small producers prefer a phone call, and English is reliable at Popova Kula, Stobi, Kamnik and Tikveš but not at every family cellar.
raw.Producers beyond wine: **Rakija**, grape *lozova rakija* and plum, is distilled at household level across the basin from **late September through November**, and several wineries and village households run visits. **Ajvar**, the roasted red-pepper relish, is made communally in **September**, when the whole country buys peppers by the crate: the Kavadarci and Negotino markets are stacked with them and any guesthouse will let you join. **Ohrid trout** (*Salmo letnica*) is protected and wild catch is banned or tightly restricted, what you are served is farmed or another species. **Bit Pazar** in Skopje is the biggest open market, with the **Old Bazaar** above it for burek, kebapi and Turkish coffee.
raw.Dishes by name: **Tavče gravče**, baked beans with red pepper in an earthenware *tava*, the national dish, best in a village *kafana* rather than a city restaurant. **Pastrmajlija**, the boat-shaped bread with cubed pork and egg, belongs to **Štip**, which holds the **Pastrmajlijada** festival there each autumn. **Selsko meso**, **shopska salad** and **turli tava** fill the rest. For benchmarks: **Restaurant Popova Kula** at Demir Kapija for the winery pairing, **Stara Kuća** or **Pivnica An** in Skopje's Old Bazaar for the traditional register.
raw.Season and timing: Harvest is **late August to early October**, Vranec last; the **Tikveš harvest festivals** in Kavadarci fall in September. **Ajvar season is September**, the pepper harvest peak. **Rakija distilling runs October-November.** The last week of September combines all three but is also when winemakers are least available, pick your priority.
raw.Transport and the sober-driving plan: The limit is **0.5 g/l, 0.0 for professionals and licences under two years**; A1 checks are frequent and fines payable on the spot. The Vardar rail line (Skopje-Veles-Gradsko-Demir Kapija-Gevgelija) is slow and infrequent, one leg, not a week. Hire a driver: Skopje operators including **Macedonia Travel** and **Wine Tour Macedonia** run English-speaking Tikveš days at roughly €150, €280 per car. Skopje taxis are metered and cheap; agree a price for intercity runs.

sources.verified: Popova Kula operating as a winery with hotel rooms, restaurant and structured tastings at Demir Kapija, with bookable tasting and dinner-plus-accommodation formats; Tikveš Winery at Kavadarci as a visitable estate founded 1885 and the largest in south-east Europe; Tikveš's position within the Povardarie/Vardar Valley wine region; the endemic status of Stanušina to the Tikveš basin.
sources.confidenceNotes: All prices are estimated bands converted at roughly 61.5 MKD to €1, the peg is stable but the tasting and room prices themselves are unconfirmed against 2026 lists and must be re-checked with Popova Kula, Tikveš, Stobi and Kamnik directly. English-language availability at smaller cellars is variable. The named Skopje driver operators and their day rates are indicative and should be verified. Ajvar and rakija sessions are informal, host-arranged activities and cannot be sold as scheduled products. The exact date of the Štip Pastrmajlijada and the Kavadarci harvest festivals moves each year. Ohrid trout regulations have changed repeatedly, confirm the current position before publishing anything about ordering it. Rental-car cross-border rules into North Macedonia vary by company and should be checked per supplier. Stobi entry prices and opening hours should be spot-checked.
